templates.title: Send a test event (HEC)
templates.description: One JSON event to the HEC event endpoint. Expect {"text":"Success","code":0}.
templates.body:
curl -sS "{{hec_url}}" \
  -H "Authorization: Splunk {{token}}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"event": {"message": "hello from curl"}}'

templates.title: Send a test event (HTTPS JSON)
templates.description: One JSON object. A JSON array or newline-delimited JSON also works; gzip with Content-Encoding: gzip.
templates.body:
curl -sS "{{nano_https_url}}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer {{token}}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message": "hello from curl"}'

templates.title: Vector: HEC sink
templates.description: Add to vector.toml and set `inputs` to your sources. Uses the `splunk_hec_logs` sink type; Vector appends /services/collector/event.
templates.body:
[sinks.nano_{{label}}]
type = "splunk_hec_logs"
inputs = ["my_source"]
endpoint = "{{base_url}}"
default_token = "{{token}}"
endpoint_target = "event"
compression = "gzip"
encoding.codec = "json"

templates.title: Vector: http sink (JSON)
templates.description: Newline-delimited JSON over HTTPS with a bearer token.
templates.body:
[sinks.nano_{{label}}]
type = "http"
inputs = ["my_source"]
uri = "{{nano_https_url}}"
method = "post"
compression = "gzip"
auth.strategy = "bearer"
auth.token = "{{token}}"
encoding.codec = "json"
framing.method = "newline_delimited"
request.headers.Content-Type = "application/x-ndjson"

templates.title: Fluent Bit: HEC output
templates.description: Add to fluent-bit.conf (HEC output plugin, `Name splunk`). TLS is required on port 443.
templates.body:
[OUTPUT]
    Name         splunk
    Match        *
    Host         {{hostname}}
    Port         443
    TLS          On
    TLS.Verify   On
    Splunk_Token {{token}}

templates.title: Fluent Bit: http output (JSON lines)
templates.description: Newline-delimited JSON over HTTPS with a bearer token.
templates.body:
[OUTPUT]
    Name        http
    Match       *
    Host        {{hostname}}
    Port        443
    URI         /ingest
    Format      json_lines
    Header      Authorization Bearer {{token}}
    TLS         On
    TLS.Verify  On

templates.title: Fluent Bit: opentelemetry output
templates.description: OTLP/HTTP protobuf logs to /v1/logs.
templates.body:
[OUTPUT]
    Name        opentelemetry
    Match       *
    Host        {{hostname}}
    Port        443
    Logs_uri    /v1/logs
    Header      Authorization Bearer {{token}}
    TLS         On
    TLS.Verify  On

templates.title: OpenTelemetry Collector: otlphttp exporter
templates.description: Add the exporter and reference it from your logs pipeline. The endpoint accepts protobuf only.
templates.body:
exporters:
  otlphttp/nano:
    logs_endpoint: {{otlp_logs_url}}
    encoding: proto
    compression: gzip
    headers:
      Authorization: "Bearer {{token}}"

service:
  pipelines:
    logs:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [otlphttp/nano]

templates.title: OpenTelemetry Collector: HEC exporter
templates.description: Sends collector logs as HEC events with the `splunk_hec` exporter.
templates.body:
exporters:
  splunk_hec/nano:
    endpoint: {{hec_url}}
    token: "{{token}}"
    tls:
      insecure_skip_verify: false

service:
  pipelines:
    logs:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [splunk_hec/nano]

templates.title: Send a test event (HEC, collector)
templates.description: Each HEC envelope declares its source in `sourcetype`. Expect {"text":"Success","code":0}.
templates.body:
# Allowed sourcetype values: {{sources}}
# An event without a sourcetype lands as unknown; any other value rejects the request (403).
curl -sS "{{hec_url}}" \
  -H "Authorization: Splunk {{token}}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"sourcetype": "{{example_source}}", "event": {"message": "hello from curl"}}'

templates.title: Send a test event (HTTPS JSON, collector)
templates.description: Declare the source per request with X-Source-Type, or per event with a `source_type` field (it wins).
templates.body:
# Allowed source values: {{sources}}
# Without X-Source-Type or source_type the event lands as unknown.
curl -sS "{{nano_https_url}}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer {{token}}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Source-Type: {{example_source}}" \
  -d '{"message": "hello from curl"}'

templates.title: Vector: HEC sink (collector)
templates.description: Set `.nano_source` on every event (a remap per source) and the `splunk_hec_logs` sink sends it as the HEC sourcetype.
templates.body:
# Allowed values for .nano_source: {{sources}}
# Events without it land as unknown; any other value rejects the batch (403).
[transforms.nano_{{label}}_source]
type = "remap"
inputs = ["my_source"]
source = '.nano_source = "{{example_source}}"'

[sinks.nano_{{label}}]
type = "splunk_hec_logs"
inputs = ["nano_{{label}}_source"]
endpoint = "{{base_url}}"
default_token = "{{token}}"
endpoint_target = "event"
sourcetype = "{{ nano_source }}"
compression = "gzip"
encoding.codec = "json"

templates.title: Vector: http sink (JSON, collector)
templates.description: Each event declares its source in a `source_type` field; set it with a remap per source.
templates.body:
# Allowed values for .source_type: {{sources}}
# Events without it land as unknown; any other value rejects the batch (403).
[transforms.nano_{{label}}_source]
type = "remap"
inputs = ["my_source"]
source = '.source_type = "{{example_source}}"'

[sinks.nano_{{label}}]
type = "http"
inputs = ["nano_{{label}}_source"]
uri = "{{nano_https_url}}"
method = "post"
compression = "gzip"
auth.strategy = "bearer"
auth.token = "{{token}}"
encoding.codec = "json"
framing.method = "newline_delimited"
request.headers.Content-Type = "application/x-ndjson"

templates.title: Fluent Bit: HEC output (collector)
templates.description: HEC output plugin (`Name splunk`). Add a nano_source key to each record (one modify filter per input) and send it as the HEC sourcetype.
templates.body:
# Allowed nano_source values: {{sources}}
# Records without it land as unknown; any other value rejects the batch (403).
[FILTER]
    Name   modify
    Match  my_source.*
    Add    nano_source {{example_source}}

[OUTPUT]
    Name                  splunk
    Match                 *
    Host                  {{hostname}}
    Port                  443
    TLS                   On
    TLS.Verify            On
    Splunk_Token          {{token}}
    Event_Sourcetype_Key  $nano_source

templates.title: Fluent Bit: http output (collector)
templates.description: Add a source_type key to each record (one modify filter per input); JSON lines over HTTPS.
templates.body:
# Allowed source_type values: {{sources}}
# Records without it land as unknown; any other value rejects the batch (403).
[FILTER]
    Name   modify
    Match  my_source.*
    Add    source_type {{example_source}}

[OUTPUT]
    Name        http
    Match       *
    Host        {{hostname}}
    Port        443
    URI         /ingest
    Format      json_lines
    Header      Authorization Bearer {{token}}
    TLS         On
    TLS.Verify  On

templates.title: Fluent Bit: opentelemetry output (collector)
templates.description: One output per source, each declaring it with the x-nano-source header.

templates.title: OpenTelemetry Collector: otlphttp exporter (collector)
templates.description: Declare the source per resource with the nano.source attribute (one resource processor per pipeline), or per exporter with the x-nano-source header. The attribute wins.
templates.body:
# Allowed nano.source values: {{sources}}
# Resources without it (and no x-nano-source header) land as unknown.
processors:
  resource/nano_source:
    attributes:
      - key: nano.source
        value: {{example_source}}
        action: upsert

exporters:
  otlphttp/nano:
    logs_endpoint: {{otlp_logs_url}}
    encoding: proto
    compression: gzip
    headers:
      Authorization: "Bearer {{token}}"
      # One source per exporter instead: x-nano-source: {{example_source}}

service:
  pipelines:
    logs:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [resource/nano_source]
      exporters: [otlphttp/nano]

templates.title: OpenTelemetry Collector: HEC exporter (collector)
templates.description: The `splunk_hec` exporter sends each record's `com.splunk.sourcetype` attribute (or the exporter default) as the HEC sourcetype.
templates.body:
# Allowed sourcetype values: {{sources}}
# Records without a sourcetype land as unknown; any other value rejects the batch (403).
exporters:
  splunk_hec/nano:
    endpoint: {{hec_url}}
    token: "{{token}}"
    sourcetype: "{{example_source}}"
    tls:
      insecure_skip_verify: false

service:
  pipelines:
    logs:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [splunk_hec/nano]

templates.description: Data > Destinations > HEC-compatible destination > Add Destination. One destination for every source; each event's sourcetype declares it.

templates.title: Cribl Stream: Webhook destination (collector)
templates.description: Data > Destinations > Webhook > Add Destination. Each event's source_type field declares its source.

templates.description: Data > Destinations > OpenTelemetry > Add Destination. Declare the source per resource (nano.source) or per destination (x-nano-source header).
